title: LTS channel support matrix and gated rollout plan for runtime/API/SDKs/Console
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic LTS channel design and a consumable support matrix that spans Runtime, Public API, Official SDKs, and Console UI, plus concrete rollout gates and upgrade tooling so customers (hosted, dedicated, private) can plan upgrades with clear compatibility guarantees.

Background: We need stable LTS channels to support enterprise customers on long upgrade cadences while enabling rapid innovation on non-LTS releases. This ticket produces the canonical LTS support matrix and an actionable gated rollout plan.

Decisions (draft):
- LTS naming: LTS-x where x increments annually (LTS-2026, LTS-2027) to avoid semantic-major confusion.
- Semantic guarantees: Runtime/exported wire protocol and Public API follow semantic versioning within an LTS: patch/backwards-compatible minor fixes allowed; breaking changes require a new LTS. SDKs will publish a compatibility table mapping SDK minor versions to runtime LTS versions. Console is treated as a consumer of the Public API and will support the last two LTS channels.
- Support window: Each LTS has a guaranteed 18-month maintenance window (security/critical fixes), plus an optional paid extended support period (12 months) for enterprise contracts.
- Upgrade path: Minor upgrades within an LTS should be zero-downtime with rolling restarts and automatic KV cache migrations. Major or cross-LTS changes require running compatibility checks and the upgrade-tooling assisted migration.

Support matrix (summary lines - canonical table will live in Confluence link):
- Runtime: supported LTS channels: current LTS (LTS-2026), previous LTS (LTS-2025) for critical fixes only. Compatible client API versions: runtime will accept requests from API minor versions N and N-1; deprecation warnings emitted in response headers.
- Public API: supported LTS channels mirror runtime; backward-compatible schema additions allowed; removal of fields only in new LTS. Version negotiation: Accepts v1.* and v2.* for overlapping window, documented per release.
- SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go): each SDK will declare supported LTSs in release notes and include a compatibility matrix artifact. SDKs must pass end-to-end regression tests against the runtime test harness gated in CI before release to LTS channel.
- Console: supports current LTS and previous LTS for dashboards and runtime control plane. Non-LTS feature flags may be hidden unless explicitly enabled.

Rollout gates and observability-driven promotion:
- Staging -> Canary (1%) -> Canary (10%) -> Progressive (50%) -> Wide (100%). Each step gated by automated checks over a 4-hour window: error rate (5xx delta threshold), p99 latency, token-generation correctness (synthetic prompts and eval prompts), SDK and API contract regressions, and customer-visible metric anomalies.
- Gate thresholds: default trigger if error-rate delta > 1.5x baseline or p99 latency increase > 20% sustained for 15 minutes. For high-risk builds (runtime or kernel changes), require additional safety: manual signoff from SRE and applied chaos test run.
- Automatic rollback: if any gate fails or there is a sudden increase in error-rate/latency, rollback to the previous stable LTS-compatible image and create an incident with a predefined runbook.

Upgrade tooling & workflows:
- Migration CLI (redwood-upgrade): assists Dedicated/Private customers to evaluate their cluster, run preflight checks, and apply staged upgrades. Outputs a compatibility report mapping installed SDKs and third-party integrations to required versions.
- In-hosted pathing: Hosted customers can pin to an LTS channel; platform will offer a one-click upgrade flow that runs synthetic checks and schedules the migration window per customer.
- CI integration: Add release-checker job that runs SDK matrix tests against runtime LTS images and publishes a compatibility artifact (JSON) that the Console and SDK package releases consume.

Compatibility guarantees (consumer-facing language):
- Within an LTS: API requests that follow documented schemas will not break. Minor and patch releases may add fields but will not remove existing fields or change semantics.
- Cross-LTS: For breaking changes, we will provide a documented migration path, a compatibility shim where feasible, SDK helpers, and at least one overlap month where both LTS channels are served to allow customer migration.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strict should runtime wire compatibility be for third-party model formats? (trade-off: strict compatibility slows model runtime improvements)
- Allocation of engineering time between LTS maintenance vs non-LTS feature velocity.
- Exact rollback thresholds for user-visible quality vs internal metrics — need iteration with SRE and product.

Next steps:
- Finalize matrix table and publish the Confluence support matrix (owner: Priya).
- Implement compatibility artifact in CI (owner: Eng Runtime team).
- Build initial redwood-upgrade MVP for dedicated/private customers (owner: Liam).
- Coordinate a PM review to align support windows and paid-extended-support terms (owner: Marcus Rivera).

Deliverables:
- Confluence: LTS support matrix + upgrade runbook.
- CI job: release-checker that publishes compatibility JSON.
- redwood-upgrade CLI MVP and hosted one-click upgrade UX spec.
